headline: Possible certification of four local Charter amendment ballot questions for the November 3, 2026 General Election ballot.
summary: The meeting may certify the final form of four local ballot questions for the Nov. 3, 2026 General Election. The questions cover term limits for the Mayor and City Council, compliance with ethics laws, and appointment of the Police and Fire Chiefs.
items: Vote to certify four local ballot questions to the Secretary of State for the Nov. 3, 2026 General Election ballot
Question 1: Mayoral term limits. Would remove the consecutive-service loophole and set a 12-year lifetime limit for Mayor (Charter section 3-400)
Question 2: City Council term limits. Would remove the consecutive-service loophole and set a 12-year lifetime limit for Council members (Charter section 2-100)

Question 3: Compliance with ethics laws. Would require all elected and appointed officers to follow relevant city and state ethics laws, and update enforcement and penalty provisions (Charter sections 8-100, 300 and 301)
Question 4: Appointment of Police and Fire Chiefs. Would have the Mayor, with approval of a majority of council members, appoint the Police Chief and Fire Chief (Charter section 4-700)
location: Central Falls City Hall, 580 Broad St. Central Falls, RI 02863

City of Central Falls 
Board of Canvassers Meeting 
Central Falls City Hall 
580 Broad St. Central Falls, RI 02863 
Tuesday, August 4, 2026 
3:00 AM  
Posted on July 31, 2026, at 11:00 PM 
 
Agenda 
 
1. Roll Call 
 
2. Pledge of Allegiance 
 
3. Items for Discussion, Vote, and/or other action (votes may be taken on all items) 
 
The Board may vote to certify to the Secretary of State the final form of local ballot 
questions to be placed on Nov. 3, 2026, General Election ballot, The four local questions, 
in accordance with the R.I. Gen. Laws 17-19-7 are:  
 (votes may be taken on all items) 
 
Central Falls 2026 Local Ballot Questions 
 
1) CHARTER AMENDMENT REGARDING MAYORAL TERM LIMITS 
Shall section 3-400 of the Charter be amended to remove the consecutive-
service loophole that currently permits unlimited lifetime service by allowing 
a Mayor to serve 8 years, sit out a term, and run again indefinitely, and 
instead establish a 12-year lifetime limit for service as Mayor? 
 
2) CHARTER AMENDMENT REGARDING CITY COUNCIL TERM LIMITS 
Shall section 2-100 of the Charter be amended to remove the consecutive-
service loophole that currently permits unlimited lifetime service by allowing 
a City Council member to serve 8 years, sit out a term, and run again 
indefinitely, and instead establish a 12-year lifetime limit for service as a City 
Council member? 
 
3) CHARTER AMENDMENT REGARDING COMPLIANCE WITH ETHICS LAWS 
Shall sections 8-100, 300 and 301 of the Charter be amended to remove 
ambiguity, clarify that all elected and appointed officers must comply with all 
relevant city and state ethics laws, and update related enforcement and 
penalty provisions accordingly? 
 
4) CHARTER AMENDMENT REGARDING APPOINTMENT OF POLICE AND FIRE 
CHIEFS 
Shall section 4-700 of the Charter be amended to provide that the Mayor, 
with the approval of a majority of members of the council, shall appoint the 
Police Chief and the Fire Chief? 
 
4. Adjournment
